visual_brief: Jengish Chokusu (Pik Pobeda) has a broad, rounded-to-flat summit crown above a huge banded north face of rock, snow and hanging ice, with a long ridge extending toward its western subsidiary summit. Classic views look up the Zvezdochka Glacier from South Inylchek basecamp or across from Khan Tengri, especially in alpenglow. Do not confuse it with Khan Tengri's sharp pyramid, the nearer snowy spires, or Pobeda West/Vazha Pshavela and Pobeda East alone.
notes: Eight distinct JPEGs, all visually checked; every long side is at least 1600 px. Preferred: c1, then c5 or c7. c2 is a grainy 1600 px film scan; c6 has substantial cloud below the visible summit. SummitPost licence wording is its page footer; no separate image-specific licence was displayed. Country Highpoints states the listed Creative Commons licence and also has an All rights reserved footer. No Wikipedia/Wikimedia or reference image used.
